acceptanceCriteria.statement: D12 tidal heating is computed from real physics and surfaced on the generated body, NO LONGER a hard zero. A tidally-heated body (close, eccentric orbit / Io-like moon) reports a real nonzero planetData.tidalHeating; a cold, distant body reports ~0. This holds for BOTH planets AND moons (the function PhysicsEngine.tidalHeating() at PhysicsEngine.js:295 was dead end-to-end — called only in tests; PlanetGenerator hard-zeroes it inline at PlanetGenerator.js:565 and MoonGenerator never calls it at all). The value is surfaced ONLY — it is NOT wired into computeSurfaceHistory (that stays its current behavior; consumption is WS2's job).

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run the WS1 tests: generate a tidally-heated planet and an Io-like moon at fixed seeds, and a cold distant body; read planetData.tidalHeating
verifyVia.observable: planetData.tidalHeating is real and >0 for the tidally-heated planet and the moon, and ~0 for the cold body; the value matches PhysicsEngine.tidalHeating() called with the body's real eccentricity/parent params; computeSurfaceHistory output is unchanged from before (resurfacing identical)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every body has a real orbital eccentricity (it was never computed — circularize() at PhysicsEngine.js:321 is dead, and orbits are circular by construction at StarSystemGenerator.js:362-363). WS1 seeds a deterministic initial eccentricity (rng, formation/zone-informed) and damps it via circularize(), surfacing planetData.eccentricity in [0,1). DATA-ONLY: eccentricity does NOT feed orbit placement in WS1 (visible orbits stay circular). It feeds AC1's tidal-heating call.

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run: generate the same body at a fixed seed twice; generate close-in vs distant bodies; read planetData.eccentricity
verifyVia.observable: planetData.eccentricity is present, in [0,1), and identical across runs of the same seed (deterministic); AC1's tidal-heating call consumes planetData.eccentricity (not a literal); orbit placement (px/pz) is unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A body's magnetic-field strength (D13) — the DYNAMO field the aurora path uses — is surfaced on planetData as a single canonical value: computed once in generate() and read by the aurora block (no longer recomputed-and-discarded there), with the surfaced number byte-identical to the aurora path's prior value (behavior-preserving). NARROWED 2026-06-24 (Max, after verify-workstream found the bind): computeAtmosphere (PhysicsEngine.js:167-168) intentionally keeps its OWN internal field-strength proxy for atmosphere stripping, which uses a cruder lock test (|rotationSpeed|<0.01, treating 3:2-resonance as fully locked) than the surfaced dynamo value (lockType==='synchronous'). Unifying them is a deliberate BEHAVIOR CHANGE (alters 3:2-resonance atmosphere retention) and is OUT of additive-WS1 scope — logged as a follow-up cleanup (see intent.md + production-L1-plan deferred cleanups). The surfaced magneticField is the canonical dynamo driver for WS2/E4.

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run: generate bodies across iron/rotation/lock combinations; read planetData.magneticField and compare to the aurora path's dynamo expression ironFraction * (lockType==='synchronous' ? 0.2 : 1.0)
verifyVia.observable: planetData.magneticField is present and EQUALS the aurora/dynamo value (single source for the aurora path; the aurora block reads it rather than recomputing); aurora rendering inputs are unchanged (surfaced value === old inline aurora value). computeAtmosphere's separate internal stripping proxy is intentionally out of scope per the narrowed AC (logged cleanup).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A body's age (D16) and its system's metallicity are surfaced on planetData. Both already exist at system level (StarSystemGenerator.js:585-586) and are consumed internally (ageGyr enters generate() at :367; metallicity feeds deriveComposition/_pickType) but are dropped from the returned object (PlanetGenerator.js:660-688). This is a ~2-line additive plumb.

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run: generate a body in a system with known ageGyr + metallicity; read planetData.age and planetData.metallicity
verifyVia.observable: planetData.age === the system ageGyr and planetData.metallicity === the system metallicity for the same generation (pure equality)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: From any generated body you can resolve its place in the system — siblings (other planets' type + orbit), its own moons, its resonance partners, and its companion star class — via a FLAT derived planetData.systemContext summary. The graph is computed one level up AFTER the body exists (planets[].moons at StarSystemGenerator.js:390/393, resonanceChain at PhysicsEngine.js:596, companion star2 at :567) and the body only carries moonCount today, so this requires a second back-link pass. It MUST be a flat summary, NOT a live back-reference (planetData._system = systemData would be circular and break JSON save/share).

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run: generate a known resonant system (>=3 compact planets); from one body read planetData.systemContext; then JSON.stringify(systemData)
verifyVia.observable: systemContext resolves real siblings (type+orbit), the body's actual moons (not just a count), resonance partners matching systemData.resonanceChain, and the companion class; JSON.stringify(systemData) succeeds with no circular-reference throw

acceptanceCriteria.statement: WS1 is strictly additive: nothing that renders today changes. For a fixed seed x type grid, the generated output is byte/tolerance-identical to before EXCEPT for the new keys (tidalHeating, eccentricity, magneticField, age, metallicity, systemContext). computeSurfaceHistory/resurfacing, orbit placement, aurora/atmosphere behavior, and the save/serialization system are all unchanged. The diff is the gate.

inputs: PhysicsEngine.tidalHeating(eccentricity, massParentEarth, radiusMoonEarth, orbitRadiusEarth) -- PhysicsEngine.js:295. Real, Io-normalized, currently called ONLY in __tests__/PhysicsEngine.test.js (dead in production for both planets and moons).

PhysicsEngine.circularize(initialEccentricity, ageGyr, orbitAU, massParent) -- PhysicsEngine.js:321. Real but dead (test-only). NOTE: no initial eccentricity is seeded anywhere -- orbits are circular by construction (StarSystemGenerator.js:362-363) -- so WS1 must SEED an initial eccentricity, then damp; it is 'compute', not 'un-comment'.

Inline magnetic fieldStrength computations: PhysicsEngine.js:168 (computeAtmosphere, ironFraction*(isLocked?0.2:1.0)) and PlanetGenerator.js:421 (aurora block, identical) -- computed twice, surfaced never.
systemData.ageGyr + systemData.metallicity (StarSystemGenerator.js:585-586) -- available, consumed internally, dropped from the body's return.

The system graph computed one level up AFTER body creation: planets[].moons (StarSystemGenerator.js:390/393), detectResonances -> resonanceChain (PhysicsEngine.js:396 -> :596), companion star2 (StarSystemGenerator.js:567). Not exposed to per-body planetData (body carries only moonCount).
PlanetGenerator.generate()'s returned planetData object (PlanetGenerator.js:660-688) -- the surface to extend with the new keys.
MoonGenerator.generate() / MoonGenerator._pickType (MoonGenerator.js:312) -- the moon path, which also never calls tidalHeating().
outputs: planetData.tidalHeating -- real, computed via PhysicsEngine.tidalHeating(), nonzero for tidally-heated bodies; surfaced for BOTH planets and moons. Surfaced ONLY (not wired into computeSurfaceHistory).
planetData.eccentricity -- a deterministic seeded-then-damped value in [0,1); data-only (not fed to orbit placement). Feeds the tidal-heating call.
planetData.magneticField (D13) -- surfaced from a single canonical computation; aurora/atmosphere read it instead of recomputing.
planetData.systemContext -- a FLAT derived summary (siblings' type+orbit, own-moons summary, resonance partners, companion class); serialization-safe (no circular reference).
WS2's Tier-1 base step / L0 adapter is the downstream consumer of all of the above -- it replaces the lab's current preset-shim self-derivation with reads of the real L0 output.
mustStayWorking: computeSurfaceHistory / surfaceHistory.resurfacing behavior -- UNCHANGED. D12 is surfaced, NOT wired into resurfacing (that re-wire is deliberately deferred to keep WS1 zero-regression and to avoid changing the deferred game renderer).
The shipped game renderer (src/objects/Planet.js) reads of surfaceHistory / crater density -- unchanged (additive scope).
Aurora/atmosphere reads of magnetic fieldStrength -- must EQUAL the now-surfaced planetData.magneticField (single source; behavior-preserving).
Orbit placement (px/pz from orbitAngle, StarSystemGenerator.js:362-363) -- unchanged; eccentricity is data-only in WS1.

The save/serialization system -- JSON.stringify(systemData) and any save/share path must still succeed; the systemContext summary must NOT introduce a circular reference (this is the load-bearing reason for a flat summary over a live back-ref).
